standard_prerequisites.name: The exact sequence of the regular model, the positivity of the intersection form and the divided special fibre
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a regular model an invertible sheaf that is trivial on the generic fibre is attached to a divisor supported on the special fibre and determined by it; the intersection form on the components is negative definite on the subspace of combinations orthogonal to the multiplicity vector, so a combination of components whose self-intersection number vanishes is a rational multiple of the multiplicity vector; and the divisor obtained by dividing the special fibre by the gcd of the multiplicities is torsion of order dividing that gcd. The author's own lemmas of this section are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the characterisation used to control the kernel in the h-torsion sequence of this section and to make the divisor of the divided special fibre explicit.

core_obligations: Use the exact sequence of the regular model to write the given sheaf as the one attached to an integral combination of the components of the special fibre, which is possible because the sheaf restricts to the trivial sheaf on the generic fibre (source lines 5898-5900).

Compute the degree hypothesis in intersection-theoretic terms: the degree of the restriction to a component is the intersection number of that component with the combination, so the hypothesis that all those degrees vanish says that the combination is orthogonal to every component, hence its self-intersection number is zero (source lines 5901-5903).

Apply the negative definiteness of the intersection form: a combination whose self-intersection number vanishes is a rational multiple of the multiplicity vector of the special fibre, and since the combination is integral that multiple is rational and the combination is an integral multiple of the divided divisor (source lines 5904-5907).

Conclude with the torsion order of the divided divisor: the sheaf is an integral power of the sheaf attached to the divided special fibre, and that sheaf has order dividing the gcd of the multiplicities, so the d-th tensor power of the original sheaf is trivial (source lines 5907-5909).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the sheaf as attached to an integral combination of components using the exact sequence of the model.
Translate the degree-zero hypotheses into the vanishing of the self-intersection number of that combination.
Use negative definiteness to identify the combination as an integral multiple of the divided special fibre.
Apply the torsion order of the divided special fibre to conclude that the d-th tensor power is trivial.
